request.spec:
A bulk settle that settles at least one claim (a claim that goes to PENDING counts) is a batch,
numbered 1, 2, ... on the sheet in the order the batches happen. Each claim settled by it shows its
batch number; a claim settled one at a time shows nothing. The screen shows the number of the last
batch beside the bulk settle button, or nothing when there has been none.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle that settles at least one claim (a claim that goes to PENDING counts) is a batch,
numbered 1, 2, ... on the sheet in the order the batches happen. Each claim settled by it shows its
batch number; a claim settled one at a time shows nothing. The screen shows the number of the last
batch beside the bulk settle button, or nothing when there has been none.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk settle batches are in, and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests. Scenario 2 also hit two bugs that were already in the app, so I fixed those as well (below).

**The batch change**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V51__settle_batch.sql`, adds `sheet.last_settle_batch` (0 means no batch yet) and `claim.settle_batch`. It also adds them to the `hist`/`asof` copies, so the as-of view still works.
- **Server:** in `SettleClaims`, the batch number is only taken when the first claim actually settles (a claim left PENDING counts). A press where every claim is refused uses up no number, and two users can't get the same one. Each claim it settles is stamped with that number.
  - Claims now carry `settleBatch` in their data.
  - A new endpoint, `GET /api/sheets/{id}/claims/settle-batch`, returns the last batch number, or null when there has been none, and respects the as-of view.
- **Screen:**
  - Each claim row has a `claim-batch` cell, which is empty for a claim settled one at a time.
  - `bulk-settle-batch` beside the "Settle selected" button shows the last batch number. It reloads whenever the claims do.
- No new audit records: the spec doesn't expect any.

A claim keeps its batch number if its status changes later. For example, a PENDING claim from a batch that is later approved on its own still shows its batch. The spec doesn't test this either way.

**Two existing bugs I fixed**
1. **Delegated users couldn't edit claims.** The screen's own viewer check (`features/claims/status.slot.tsx`) ignored delegations. A viewer acting for a steward was blocked from editing a claim, even though the server allows it. The check now follows the server's rule: the delegation must come from a steward and cover the sheet's today.
2. **A refused quick-add still created the person.** When a quick-add for a new name was refused because the date fell in a closed period, the new person was saved anyway. `ResolvePerson` now runs the closed-period check before adding the person, so a refusal leaves nothing behind.

This doesn't explain why the transaction didn't undo the person on refusal. Other endpoints that save something and then refuse might have the same problem; I didn't look into that.
